reviews.question: Which statements are true for ideal truss design? (i) Loads act at joints. (ii) Members are joined by smooth pins. (iii) Each member is a single-force member.
reviews.explanation: A truss consists of members arranged in connected triangles so the assembly behaves as one object. Its web of triangles distributes loads and permits changing tension and compression without idealised member bending or shearing. Loads are applied at joints where members connect through smooth pins. Each member is a two-force member,with equal and opposite forces,either tension or compression,at its two ends. reviews.sourceExplanation: A truss consists of members organised into connected triangles so the overall assembly behaves as a single object. Its web of triangles enables even distribution of weight and handling changing tension and compression without bending or shearing. All loads are applied at points where members are joined by smooth pins. Each truss member acts as a double-force member with equal and opposite force,either tension or compression,at both ends.
